text_copy: AUDIT/primary/fechner2019-cocoa-origin-al-cd-exposure.txt (pdftotext -layout); earlier HTML/XML copies AUDIT/primary/fechner2019.{txt,xml,html} not needed
disposition_reason: BfR exposure paper that reports German Food Monitoring (GFM) Al and Cd concentrations in 167/166 retail cocoa powders, by declared origin (Table 2), by theoretical concentration segments (Table 3) and by year (Table 4), plus Eurostat trade flows and package origin labelling.

study.design: monitoring summary (secondary analysis of German Food Monitoring) + dietary exposure assessment
study.material_scope: retail cocoa powder (weakly fat-reduced, strongly fat-reduced or unspecified); cocoa mass excluded from occurrence because fewer samples
study.growing_origin_vs_market: All samples from German official monitoring (purchase market Germany). Declared origins are mostly NOT growing origins: European/Russian declarations likely reflect processing/packaging country; only 12 samples (Africa, Côte d'Ivoire, Bolivia, Dominican Republic, Peru, Indonesia) have FAO-plausible cultivation origins. Eurostat: German cocoa beans/powder/mass mainly from Côte d'Ivoire, with the Netherlands the main distributor.
study.collection_period: GFM monitoring window 2005-2015; cocoa powder was analysed in 2008 (Al n=80, Cd n=79) and 2012 (n=87).
study.sampling_unit: individual retail cocoa-powder samples (official food monitoring); 167 for Al, 166 for Cd
study.method: GFAAS or ICP-MS (GFM codes Al ss-1813000, Cd ss-1848000); digestion not described
study.lod_loq: Not reported; all samples stated quantifiable
study.basis: cocoa powder as sold/tested (mixed weakly fat-reduced, strongly fat-reduced and unspecified cocoa powder; no dry-matter or fat-free normalisation reported)

findings.material: cocoa powder (GFM code el-450401; weakly/strongly fat-reduced or unspecified, summarised)
findings.basis: cocoa powder as sold/tested (mixed weakly fat-reduced, strongly fat-reduced and unspecified cocoa powder; no dry-matter or fat-free normalisation reported)
findings.censoring: Source states all cocoa-powder samples analysed for Al and Cd had quantifiable concentrations (no non-detects); LOD/LOQ not reported.
findings.locator: Table 2, p.8, row "European origins summarised", Al N/Mean/SD
findings.notes: GFM origin declaration that is NOT a cocoa cultivation area; authors state such declarations (esp. Germany) likely name the place of processing/packaging, not growing origin. All samples were taken in German official food monitoring, so the purchase market is Germany in every case; group_kind=purchase_market is used only to flag that this is not a growing origin. Table footnote: for most origins sample numbers are low and statistically not significant.

controls.control: Integrate plausible cocoa origin information (origin labelling / origin-specific sampling) into exposure assessment and sampling
controls.comparator: Standard scenarios (all-sample mean/P95) vs origin-related scenarios using concentration-segment means (theoretical origin A/B)
controls.outcome: Highest P95 exposure: scenario 4 (all-sample P95 conc.) Al 0.152 mg/week/kg BW and Cd 0.363 µg/week/kg BW (~15% of TWI each); origin-B scenario 8: Al 0.136-0.142 mg/week/kg BW (14% TWI), Cd 0.203-0.230 µg/week/kg BW (8-9% TWI). Origin A and B are concentration tertiles/quartiles, not real origins, so no measured origin effect.

controls.control: Mandatory country-of-origin labelling for processed cocoa products (recommendation)
controls.comparator: Voluntary labelling: of 14 cocoa powders launched in Germany Jan 1996-May 2018 (Mintel GNPD), 5 conventional had no origin, 2 said West Africa, 1 "nederland kakao", 3 organic said non-EU, 3 organic named Ecuador, Dominican Republic/South America, Indonesia
controls.outcome: Authors conclude mandatory origin labelling is needed to integrate origin into exposure assessment; no concentration outcome.

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary lists "12,482 cocoa-powder consumers"; Table 1 gives 12,115 cocoa-powder consumers, 3,802 cocoa-mass consumers and 12,482 for cocoa sum.

Stored summary says scenario 4 Cd is 14% of TWI and "Cd at P95 was substantially lower as a fraction of TWI than Al"; the paper states scenario 4 represented 15% of the TWI for both Al and Cd (0.363/2.5 = 14.5%).
Stored summary does not mention the occurrence tables (Tables 2-4) at all; the key concentration data (all-sample Al mean 146 mg/kg, P95 223; Cd mean 0.19 mg/kg, P95 0.53) are missing.
Stored summary calls the 2005-2015 window the data period; actual cocoa powder analyses were only in 2008 and 2012.
unresolved: LOD/LOQ, digestion method and QA (CRM/recovery) not reported in the paper; GFAAS vs ICP-MS split per sample unknown.
Fat-content split not available; basis cannot be normalised to fat-free or dry matter.
Declared European origins (incl. Germany n=114) cannot be mapped to growing origins; only 12 samples have plausible cultivation origins and most of those are n=1-2.

group_kind values "concentration_segment" (Table 3 origin A/B) is outside the schema enum; "all_samples" used for the not-specified subset and "purchase_market" used for non-cultivation declared origins as nearest fits.
n=1 Table 2 rows are entered both as findings (statistic sample_value) and in sample_values; do not double count.
